content: Prescription drug prices for single-source brand-name medications in the United States are significantly higher compared to those in Canada and other countries, many of which implement price controls. However, the prices for generic drugs tend to be higher in Canada than in the United States. A considerable number of older Americans travel to Canada or purchase their medications online from Canadian pharmacies to save 50% or more on essential drugs. Pharmaceutical companies argue that the high prices they set are necessary to sustain funding for research and development. Only 11% of drug candidates that enter clinical trials successfully receive approval for sale. The substantial costs associated with conducting clinical trials for unsuccessful drug candidates must be recouped through the sales of successful drugs. Without this, the discovery and development of new pharmaceutical drugs would become unsustainable. Prescription drug prices, particularly in the context of Medicare, have become a contentious political issue in the United States. Drug companies and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulators claim that there are potential risks to consumers who use drugs imported from Canada. However, there is skepticism regarding the actual level of risk involved. Both houses of Congress have passed legislation to allow drug imports, but the Bush Administration and the FDA have opposed such measures. Anticipated Medicare reforms, which are expected to pass, include prescription drug coverage under Medicare. There is also some interest in Congress in permitting drug imports under FDA regulation to provide medications at reduced rates to consumers in need.
